item.description:
**Download:** [Leise-2.2.0.zip](https://github.com/ramonfeng/leise/releases/download/v2.2.0/Leise-2.2.0.zip) — quit Leise, then replace the old `Leise.app` in your Applications folder. (First launch after replacing: System Settings → Privacy & Security → "Open Anyway", same as before — [README](https://github.com/ramonfeng/leise#readme).)
## What changed in 2.2.0
- **File names like `Claude.md` survive dictation.** The streaming pipeline was cutting dictated dots at sentence boundaries, so a phrase like „Claude Punkt md" reached the polish stage in pieces and came out as `cloud。 md` / `Claude 的。 md` / the word `DOT` — several shapes of the same failure. The delivery layer now rejoins exactly those orphans (guided by how the dot was actually spoken) and leaves true sentence endings alone. - **The Dictionary → Replacements tab no longer crashes.** Two replacement rules that had been stored without an internal identifier crashed that tab on scroll; the stored data has been repaired and the app made structurally immune to that failure mode. - **Leise is called Leise.** The menu bar and some system dialogs still introduced the app by its internal build name; every user-visible name is now simply Leise. - **The setup guide respects what you have already answered.** Replaying it no longer re-asks questions you have settled, finishing it no longer brings it back after a restart, and the guided recording test now describes *your* hotkey gesture — if your shortcut is press-once-start, press-again-stop, that is what it says. - **Update checks (introduced in 2.1.36) are hardened.** The consent question can no longer re-appear after you have answered it, and enabling or disabling the toggle gives immediate, visible confirmation.
If you are coming from 2.1.34 or earlier, 2.2.0 also contains everything from the intermediate 2.1.35/2.1.36 releases: the first-launch window that listed all your apps is gone (the installation completes itself instead), the recordings dialog simply asks, and update checks are available on your terms.
## The essentials (unchanged)
**Apple Silicon only** (M1 or newer) · **macOS 14.4+** · about **7 GB free disk** (523 MB app + 5.9 GB speech models downloaded on first run).
A 100 % local dictation app for macOS. Your audio and your transcripts never leave your Mac; it works with the network off.
**macOS will refuse to open it once.** Leise is signed but not notarised. ⛔ **In both dialogs the blue default button is "Move to Trash"** — pressing Return deletes the app you just downloaded. Click **Done**, then go to **System Settings → Privacy & Security**, find the line about Leise, and click **Open Anyway**. Full walkthrough in English, Deutsch and 简体中文: [README](https://github.com/ramonfeng/leise#readme).
**What it sends over the network.** Nothing about you. The speech models on first run, and — only if you enable update checks, which ships off — a version-number request to the update feed. Both under your control.
Anything wrong: **Settings → General → Diagnostics → Export Diagnostics** writes a file to your Downloads folder. Send it over.
